title: Given K sorted arrays, merge them into a single sorted array. Explain the K-way Merge technique with a heap, the complexity, and a banking use case.
shortTitle: Merge K Sorted Arrays (Combine K Sorted Arrays into One Sorted Array)
keyPoints: Each heap entry carries the value, the array index, and the element index to locate the successor.
The heap holds at most K candidates at any time, one per array.
Each of the N total elements is pushed and popped exactly once at O(log K) cost.
Total time is O(N log K), strictly better than O(N log N) re-sorting when K is small.
Pre-sizing the output array to the known total avoids repeated resizing.
This is the array form of the K-way Merge pattern used for sorted linked lists.

s1_definition.oneliner: Seed a min-heap with one element per array, pop the global minimum into the output, and push the successor from the same array.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Merge K Sorted Arrays** is the array form of the K-way Merge pattern.
- Each heap entry stores `{value, arrayIndex, elementIndex}` to track the source.
- We **seed** the heap with the first element of each non-empty array.
- We repeatedly **pop** the global minimum into the output and **push** the next element from the same array.
- The heap holds at most **K** candidates at any time.
- Time is **O(N log K)** and space is **O(K)** for the heap plus **O(N)** for the output.
s1_definition.analogy: The National Bank of India has K sorted arrays of daily settlement amounts, one per processing desk. To build one chronological settlement sheet for reconciliation, a clerk keeps the earliest unused amount from each desk on a tray, writes the smallest one to the sheet, and pulls the next amount from that same desk. The tray never holds more than K slips.

sections.s6_takeaway:
Merge K Sorted Arrays is the array form of the K-way Merge pattern. Because arrays have no next pointer, each heap entry carries the value together with the array index and the element index, so after popping a value you can fetch its successor in the same array. You seed the min-heap with the first element of every non-empty array, then repeatedly pop the global minimum into the output and push the next element from whichever array you just drew from.

The efficiency argument is that the heap holds at most K candidates, so each of the N total elements is pushed and popped once at O(log K) cost, giving O(N log K) overall. This is strictly better than the O(N log N) of collecting everything and re-sorting, especially when K is small. Pre-sizing the output array to the known total avoids dynamic resizing overhead.

At the National Bank of India, Rajesh used this to build one end-of-day settlement sheet from several processing desks, each of which already produced its amounts in sorted order. The heap drained elements from all desks into a single sorted array for reconciliation, and the O(N log K) performance handled large settlement volumes efficiently.

The senior-level insight is understanding that the heap entry must carry source metadata (array index and element index), that the heap stays bounded by K, and that this is the same core operation used in external merge sort on disk. Explaining these points shows an interviewer you apply the K-way Merge pattern correctly to arrays.

Remember one sentence: seed a min-heap with one element per array, pop the smallest into the output, push its successor, and repeat for O(N log K) total work.
